jobs.title: Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme
jobs.description:
Kenya

Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme

Organization

International Union for Conservation of Nature

Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 22 Sep 2026

Terms of Reference

Title: Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme

Objective of the Consultancy

This Consultancy Has The Following Objective(s)

Overall Objective

To conduct a comprehensive baseline assessment and Results Framework validation for the CREATES Programme to establish credible baseline values, validate programme indicators and measurement approaches, and provide an evidence base for effective programme implementation, monitoring, learning, evaluation and adaptive management.

Specific Objectives

The consultancy shall specifically**:**

Establish baseline values for all indicators in the CREATES Results Framework using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods.
Validate the programme Results Framework, including indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, data sources, assumptions, and means of verification, and recommend improvements where necessary.
Establish basin-level baseline values for the programme's impact indicator on Achievement of SDG Target 6.5 on Transboundary Water Management, including assessment of the four contributing scoring dimensions.
Assess the feasibility of achieving the targeted basin level 10% improvement contribution to the SDG 6.5 impact indicator and recommend strategic areas of focus to maximise programme results.
Validate existing programme data from stakeholders’ workshops and ground truthing and assess its quality, reliability, and suitability for establishing programme baselines.
Generate evidence-based recommendations to strengthen programme monitoring, data management, adaptive management, learning, evaluation and results measurement throughout the programme implementation period.

Background

Project Reference: P04608

About IUCN

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

www.iucn.org

https://twitter.com/IUCN/

About The Project

The Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme is a five-year regional initiative (2026-2030) funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark with a budget of DKK 300 million as Denmark's contribution to the European Union's Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on Transboundary Water Management (TWM) in Africa. The programme seeks to improve the effectiveness of transboundary water management in Eastern Africa to enhance water security, climate resilience, regional cooperation, and sustainable development in selected transboundary river basins.

CREATES is implemented jointly by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and UNEP-DHI Centre for Water and Environment through two complementary projects that collectively contribute to a common programme objective. The programme focuses on two transboundary river basins: the Mara Basin, shared between Kenya and Tanzania, and the Sio-Malaba-Malakisi (SMM) Basin, shared between Kenya and Uganda. These basins were selected due to their ecological significance, socio-economic importance, existing transboundary cooperation mechanisms, and the urgent need to strengthen climate-resilient and sustainable water resources management.

The programme responds to persistent challenges affecting transboundary water management in Eastern Africa, including inadequate hydrological and environmental data, limited decision-support systems, weak institutional and governance capacities, insufficient cross-border coordination, inadequate financing for transboundary water investments, and low adoption of climate-resilient Nature-based Solutions (NbS). Through strengthening institutional capacity, improving access to decision-support tools and knowledge, enhancing governance arrangements, promoting collaborative water resources management, and supporting investments in climate-resilient water infrastructure and NbS, CREATES aims to contribute to improved water security and resilience across the target basins.

The Programme seeks to achieve the following four immediate outcomes:

Outcome A1: Water agencies, River Basin Organisations (RBOs), and regional bodies conduct effective climate-resilient transboundary water resources management through improved technical capacity and decision-support tools.
Outcome A2: Water agencies, RBOs and regional bodies implement and share improved climate-resilient Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) practices.
Outcome B1: Governance arrangements for transboundary water management are strengthened, enabling institutions to effectively deliver on their mandates, operationalise policy and regulatory frameworks, mobilise resources, and support policy dialogue and conflict prevention.
Outcome B2: Climate-resilient water infrastructure combined with Nature-based Solutions contributes to inclusive and sustainable water management and economic development within targeted river basins and communities.

Description Of The Assignment

Purpose

The purpose of the baseline assessment is to establish a comprehensive and credible evidence base to inform the implementation, monitoring, adaptive management, learning, and evaluation of the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme over its implementation period.

Specifically, the baseline assessment will establish baseline values for all indicators contained in the CREATES Results Framework, validate the programme's indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, data sources, assumptions, and targets, and assess the availability, quality, and reliability of existing data to support results-based management.

The Assessment Will Also Establish Basin-level Baseline Values For The Programme's Impact Indicator On Achievement Of SDG Target 6.5 On Transboundary Water Management Using The Programme-specific SDG 6.5 Transboundary Assessment Methodology. The Assessment Will Calculate The Impact Indicator As The Average Of The Transboundary-related Scores Under SDG 6.5.1 And The SDG 6.5.2 Scores. For Each Target Basin, The Assessment Shall Determine The Transboundary-related Score Based On The Four Transboundary Dimensions Of The SDG 6.5.1 Survey, Namely

Arrangements for transboundary cooperation,
Organisational framework,
Data and information sharing, and
Financing for transboundary cooperation.

In addition, the consultancy will assess the feasibility of achieving the programme's targeted 10% improvement in the impact indicator by analysing the performance of each scoring dimension, identifying key drivers, gaps, and constraints, and recommending strategic areas of focus to maximise programme impact and contribute to improved transboundary water management.

The baseline assessment will further validate existing programme data and evidence, generate robust quantitative and qualitative baseline information across the programme's intervention areas, and provide recommendations to strengthen the Results Framework, indicator measurement, data collection methodologies, and monitoring systems. The findings will serve as the reference point against which programme progress, performance, outcomes, and impact will be measured throughout the life of the CREATES Programme, while also informing evidence-based decision-making, adaptive management, continuous learning, and programme improvement.

Scope of the Assignment

The consultancy shall undertake a comprehensive baseline assessment and Results Framework validation for the CREATES Programme covering all programme outcomes, outputs, and indicators across the programme implementation areas in the Mara and Sio-Malaba-Malakisi (SMM) transboundary river basins. The assignment shall adopt a regional perspective and encompass relevant stakeholders at regional, national, basin, sub-national, and community levels, as appropriate.

The scope of the consultancy shall include the following activities, but not be limited to:

Review of Programme Documentation

Undertake a comprehensive review of all relevant programme documentation to develop a thorough understanding of the programme design, implementation approach, results framework, theory of change, monitoring framework, and existing evidence.

Baseline Assessment

The consultancy shall establish baseline values for all indicators contained in the CREATES Results Framework using robust qualitative and quantitative methods. The assessment shall generate reliable baseline information against which programme progress and results will be measured throughout the implementation period. Where baseline information already exists, the consultant shall validate its quality, relevance, completeness, and applicability before recommending its adoption or proposing updated baseline values based on evidence generated during the assessment.

Results Framework and Indicator Validation

Informed by evidence from the data collected during baseline assessment, the consultancy in consultation with CREATES programme team and MEL team shall review and validate the programme Results Framework to ensure that indicators are clearly defined, measurable, practical, and aligned with the programme's intended results. This shall include verification of indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, means of verification, data sources, assumptions, disaggregation requirements, frequency of data collection, and calculation methods. The consultant shall also develop or refine Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) for all programme indicators to ensure standardised indicator definitions and measurement. Where necessary, the consultant shall recommend revisions to strengthen the Results Framework while maintaining alignment with the approved programme design.

SDG 6.5 Impact Indicator Assessment

The consultancy shall establish basin-level baseline values for the programme's impact indicator, Achievement of SDG Target 6.5 on Transboundary Water Management, using the programme-specific methodology derived from the SDG 6.5 monitoring framework. The assessment shall establish baseline scores for each target basin by analysing the transboundary-related dimensions of SDG Indicator 6.5.1 together with the SDG Indicator 6.5.2 scores to generate the overall programme impact baseline.

HETI has a great opportunity for a Senior Geologist/Senior Environmental Scientist/Senior Engineer with 10+ years’ experience in the environmental field.

This role will be responsible for providing technical and business skills and contribute to advanced solutions in the environmental, chemical, commercial, manufacturing, government, energy, financial, insurance, and/or legal sectors. This job is 100% remote.

The candidate should have experience managing consulting assignments, must work effectively in multi-disciplinary teams, is expected to be proficient in the analysis and communication of information, and must be able to work cooperatively with agencies, organizations, and individuals to guide decision-making. The successful candidate is also expected to be proficient in all facets of project management. He/she must demonstrate collaboration with colleagues throughout the organization.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Client Management & Communication:

Serve as the primary point of contact for clients and stakeholders, providing regular updates on project status and outcomes.
Collaborate with project teams, including environmental engineers, geologists, and technicians.
Communicate complex technical information to clients and stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.

Regulatory Compliance & Reporting:

Interact and coordinate with regulatory agencies to obtain necessary approvals, permits, and closure documentation.
Prepare and submit comprehensive reports, including site investigation reports, risk assessment reports, remedial action plans, progress reports, and closure reports.
Be current and continue to be current on environmental regulations and guidelines.

Remediation Planning/Implementation:

Develop and implement effective remediation plans based on the findings of site investigations and risk assessments.
Design and oversee the implementation of remediation strategies, which may include excavation, soil vapor extraction, groundwater treatment, in-situ bioremediation, or other appropriate methods.
Ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and permits during the remediation process.

Insurance Claim Support

Experience providing technical support to insurance claims professionals for environmental or energy related claims.
Understanding of insurance terminology and policy language.
Experience in assessing the source and timing of pollution events.
Diverse environmental consulting experience.
Excellent technical writing skills.

Site Assessments:

Manage/conduct comprehensive site investigations to identify potential sources of contamination, evaluate risks, and develop appropriate remediation strategies.
Collect soil, groundwater, and other environmental samples and analyze them in accordance with standard protocols and regulations.
Perform data interpretation, risk assessment, and modeling to determine the extent and nature of contamination and its potential impact on human health and the environment.

Quality Control:

Implement quality control and assurance measures to ensure accurate and reliable data collection, analysis, and reporting.
Conduct periodic audits and reviews of project activities to verify compliance with project plans and regulations.
Identify and address any deviations or discrepancies in project execution promptly.

The Ideal Candidate should have:

Current PE or PG license
Bachelor’s Degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, or a related field.
10+ years’ experience conducting site investigations remediation and third party evaluations
Solid understanding of environmental regulations, guidelines, and best practices related to contaminated site cleanup.
Excellent project management skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with clients, regulatory agencies, and project teams.
Attention to detail, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
Knowledge of environmental sampling techniques and laboratory analysis methods.

Founded in 1986, HETI is a full-service, nationwide environmental services company specializing in environmental and indoor air quality site assessment, site remediation, risk characterization, occupational health and safety services, and litigation/expert witness support. Through our network of offices throughout the U.S., we serve a variety of large and small businesses.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and offer a competitive benefit package including base salary plus bonus opportunities and a friendly, flexible work environment.

Flexible work from home options available.

jobs.description:
ERM
is hiring an Environmental
Compliance Technician
to support a key clients project in Morgantown, Maryland .
In this role, you will perform and document environmental inspections of facilities and operating areas and perform corrective actions. This is a full time (40 hours per week) limited-term role with a duration of 6 months, renewable.

Responsibilities

Water management, transfer water from various sumps and pipes to pons, conduct compliance sampling and inspections.
Perform and document environmental inspections of various onsite facilities and operating areas and record observations using inspection forms.
The inspections support compliance with environmental regulations concerning spill prevention, wastewater, stormwater, storage tanks, and waste management.
As requested, collect samples of stormwater at designated locations and visually inspect the quality of the sample.
Measure water elevations and collect water samples from onsite wells.
As needed, address minor mechanical issues (i.e. remove and replace tank appurtenances, drain secondary containment, repair/replace rain gauge, replace drum lid, etc.).
Perform work safely, complying with ERM and client requirements and wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times, including hardhat, safety boots, safety glasses, hearing protection, and orange high-visibility vest.

Communicate with ERM Project Manager, various regulatory agencies, and client staff and subcontracts at the various client facilities. Key aspect of work is to develop relationship with client personnel at the facilities to promote environmental stewardship.

Requirements

Minimum 4 years of field experience required.
Bachelor’s Degree preferred – more important is training with trades, mechanical pumps etc .
Hazwoper certification preferred.
Previous data center, power plant or BESS experience a plus.
A working vehicle, valid driver’s license, and a good driving record; ability to drive to the various project locations. Ability to rent a vehicle.
Effective observational and organization skills; experience recording detailed technical data a plus.
Effective communication skills with ERM and client staff.
Knowledge and experience with Stormwater MSGP requirements, SPCC requirements and waste tracking.
Experience operating water pumps piping and basic mechanical skills.
Experience with water and soil sample collection a plus.
Proficient in basic computer skills (i.e. Microsoft Outlook, Work, Excel) for communication and preparation of inspection documentation.
Local candidates preferred.

jobs.title: Structural Conservation Senior Specialist
jobs.location: Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
jobs.description:
We are currently looking for a Structural Conservation Senior Specialist
to join the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi.

The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) drives the sustainable growth of Abu Dhabi’s culture and tourism sectors. Through its work in cultural heritage, museums, historic environments, creative industries, and destination development, DCT Abu Dhabi plays a central role in preserving the emirate’s cultural identity while positioning Abu Dhabi as a leading global destination for culture and tourism.

Role Purpose

Lead the independent technical review, validation, and governance of structural assessments, material investigations, analytical models, and intervention strategies for modern heritage buildings across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Monitor and supervise structural interventions as required.

Key Responsibilities

Operations

Lead the technical review, validation, and quality assurance of structural assessments, material testing programmes, analytical models, conservation studies, and intervention strategies for modern heritage buildings, sites, districts, and urban heritage landscapes.
Assess and interpret the structural behaviour of existing modern heritage buildings, considering material degradation, historical construction practices, incomplete documentation, condition assessments, building pathology investigations, and historic fabric analysis.
Review and challenge consultant methodologies, assumptions, site inspection findings, testing results, analytical outputs, and recommendations to ensure conclusions are reliable, proportionate, technically sound, and aligned with conservation principles.
Evaluate and validate repair, strengthening, retrofitting, restoration, rehabilitation, adaptive reuse, and other conservation intervention strategies, ensuring minimal intervention, compatibility with existing materials, long-term durability, and preservation of heritage value.
Promote evidence-based and performance-based assessment and design approaches, including ASCE 41 where appropriate, particularly where prescriptive code compliance may lead to unnecessary interventions.
Ensure proposed interventions balance structural safety requirements with the preservation of authenticity, integrity, architectural character, character-defining features, historic urban character, scale, streetscapes, cultural values, and original material fabric.
Review and provide formal technical recommendations on structural submissions, including technical reports, review notes, presentations, specifications, method statements, restoration drawings, intervention guidelines, material treatments, and repair approaches.
Support the management of a portfolio of modern heritage assets under assessment by identifying priorities, risks, inconsistencies, feasibility requirements, viability considerations, cost implications, procurement needs, and adaptation or intervention proposals.
Supervise and provide technical input on site works related to structural improvements and conservation interventions, including monitoring structural status, site activities, logistics, mobilisation, and compliance with approved methodologies and DCT requirements.
Plan, advise, direct, and implement preventive and curative conservation interventions on registered modern architectural heritage, in coordination with relevant DCT functions, external consultants, and contractors.

Monitoring, Maintenance and Risk Management

Plan, manage, implement, monitor, maintain, and report on modern heritage sites in accordance with approved cyclical maintenance plans.
Coordinate condition monitoring, compliance monitoring, risk identification, enforcement recommendations, emergency planning, and corrective actions for deteriorated, abandoned, or at-risk modern heritage assets.

Policies, Processes and Procedures

Lead and contribute to the development of technical review frameworks, guidelines, procedures, quality standards, templates, and documentation standards for structural assessment and conservation engineering of modern heritage assets.
Provide technical expertise in defining acceptable approaches to code application for existing and heritage structures, including performance-based alternatives aligned with DCT objectives and international best practice.
Ensure technical reviews, outputs, and activities comply with relevant DCT policies, HED processes and procedures, international standards, and regulatory requirements.
Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to strengthen internal processes, review mechanisms, and operational efficiency.

Collaboration and Day-to-Day Operations

Collaborate with internal teams, external consultants, contractors, municipalities, regulatory authorities, academic institutions, and external partners on technical matters related to structural assessments, conservation interventions, policy implementation, and urban heritage revitalisation.
Support technical discussions with stakeholders and provide clear, defensible engineering positions for decision-making and project delivery.
Coordinate logistical operations related to permissions and site access for planned studies with site owners and stakeholders.
Maintain structured records of technical reviews, decisions, and supporting documentation in line with DCT requirements.

Research, Awareness and Capacity Building

Lead or contribute to research, innovation, publications, training materials, educational programmes, awareness initiatives, and supporting collateral related to modern heritage conservation, modern building materials, technologies, and capacity building.
Build internal and external awareness of appropriate structural engineering and conservation approaches for modern heritage buildings.
Respond to ad hoc requests related to modern heritage, conservation advice, reporting, stakeholder support, cross-functional initiatives, and any other duties assigned by the direct manager.
Contribute to the dissemination of knowledge within DCT and with relevant external partners, including workshops, technical forums, professional conferences, and academic events, as directed.

EHS (Environment, Health and Safety)

Comply with all relevant EHS policies, procedures, guidelines, and controls; report incidents and hazards in a timely manner; support employee safety and legislative compliance; and reduce consumption of natural resources to protect the environment and ensure a healthy and safe work environment.

Shared Activity

Follow all relevant departmental policies, processes, standard operating procedures, and instructions.
Demonstrate compliance with organisational values, ethics, and EHS requirements.
Support a culture of change management through a hands-on and can-do approach to DCT’s business opportunities, initiatives, planned targets, and high-performance behaviours.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or Structural Engineering.
Master’s Degree in Structural Engineering.
Professional certifications or memberships, such as PE, are an advantage.
6-8 years of experience in concrete repair and durability engineering, including corrosion mitigation and cathodic protection systems.
Experience in structural condition assessment of existing and ageing structures, structural modelling, and advanced analysis.
Knowledge of applicable codes and standards, including ADIBC/UAE regulations, ACI 318, ACI 562, ASCE 7, IEBC, and ASCE 41.
Proficiency with the following: ETABS, SAFE, SAP2000, AutoCAD, Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, etc.
Language competency in English is required; Arabic proficiency is preferred.

Skills

Technical expertise in structural assessment, material testing, analytical modelling, concrete durability, and repair strategy review.
Ability to interpret testing results and correlate findings with structural performance.
Strong judgment in reviewing consultant submissions and producing clear, defensible technical recommendations.
Knowledge of conservation principles, minimal intervention, material compatibility, and long-term durability for modern heritage structures.
Proficiency in technical reporting, documentation, stakeholder coordination, and structured record management.
Strong communication, collaboration, analytical thinking, problem-solving, and project coordination skills.

Interested candidates are welcome to apply or share their CV for consideration.

new_jobs.title: Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme
new_jobs.description:
Kenya

Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme

Organization

International Union for Conservation of Nature

Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 22 Sep 2026

Terms of Reference

Title: Baseline Assessment for the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme

Objective of the Consultancy

This Consultancy Has The Following Objective(s)

Overall Objective

To conduct a comprehensive baseline assessment and Results Framework validation for the CREATES Programme to establish credible baseline values, validate programme indicators and measurement approaches, and provide an evidence base for effective programme implementation, monitoring, learning, evaluation and adaptive management.

Specific Objectives

The consultancy shall specifically**:**

Establish baseline values for all indicators in the CREATES Results Framework using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods.
Validate the programme Results Framework, including indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, data sources, assumptions, and means of verification, and recommend improvements where necessary.
Establish basin-level baseline values for the programme's impact indicator on Achievement of SDG Target 6.5 on Transboundary Water Management, including assessment of the four contributing scoring dimensions.
Assess the feasibility of achieving the targeted basin level 10% improvement contribution to the SDG 6.5 impact indicator and recommend strategic areas of focus to maximise programme results.
Validate existing programme data from stakeholders’ workshops and ground truthing and assess its quality, reliability, and suitability for establishing programme baselines.
Generate evidence-based recommendations to strengthen programme monitoring, data management, adaptive management, learning, evaluation and results measurement throughout the programme implementation period.

Background

Project Reference: P04608

About IUCN

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

www.iucn.org

https://twitter.com/IUCN/

About The Project

The Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme is a five-year regional initiative (2026-2030) funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark with a budget of DKK 300 million as Denmark's contribution to the European Union's Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on Transboundary Water Management (TWM) in Africa. The programme seeks to improve the effectiveness of transboundary water management in Eastern Africa to enhance water security, climate resilience, regional cooperation, and sustainable development in selected transboundary river basins.

CREATES is implemented jointly by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and UNEP-DHI Centre for Water and Environment through two complementary projects that collectively contribute to a common programme objective. The programme focuses on two transboundary river basins: the Mara Basin, shared between Kenya and Tanzania, and the Sio-Malaba-Malakisi (SMM) Basin, shared between Kenya and Uganda. These basins were selected due to their ecological significance, socio-economic importance, existing transboundary cooperation mechanisms, and the urgent need to strengthen climate-resilient and sustainable water resources management.

The programme responds to persistent challenges affecting transboundary water management in Eastern Africa, including inadequate hydrological and environmental data, limited decision-support systems, weak institutional and governance capacities, insufficient cross-border coordination, inadequate financing for transboundary water investments, and low adoption of climate-resilient Nature-based Solutions (NbS). Through strengthening institutional capacity, improving access to decision-support tools and knowledge, enhancing governance arrangements, promoting collaborative water resources management, and supporting investments in climate-resilient water infrastructure and NbS, CREATES aims to contribute to improved water security and resilience across the target basins.

The Programme seeks to achieve the following four immediate outcomes:

Outcome A1: Water agencies, River Basin Organisations (RBOs), and regional bodies conduct effective climate-resilient transboundary water resources management through improved technical capacity and decision-support tools.
Outcome A2: Water agencies, RBOs and regional bodies implement and share improved climate-resilient Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) practices.
Outcome B1: Governance arrangements for transboundary water management are strengthened, enabling institutions to effectively deliver on their mandates, operationalise policy and regulatory frameworks, mobilise resources, and support policy dialogue and conflict prevention.
Outcome B2: Climate-resilient water infrastructure combined with Nature-based Solutions contributes to inclusive and sustainable water management and economic development within targeted river basins and communities.

Description Of The Assignment

Purpose

The purpose of the baseline assessment is to establish a comprehensive and credible evidence base to inform the implementation, monitoring, adaptive management, learning, and evaluation of the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme over its implementation period.

Specifically, the baseline assessment will establish baseline values for all indicators contained in the CREATES Results Framework, validate the programme's indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, data sources, assumptions, and targets, and assess the availability, quality, and reliability of existing data to support results-based management.

The Assessment Will Also Establish Basin-level Baseline Values For The Programme's Impact Indicator On Achievement Of SDG Target 6.5 On Transboundary Water Management Using The Programme-specific SDG 6.5 Transboundary Assessment Methodology. The Assessment Will Calculate The Impact Indicator As The Average Of The Transboundary-related Scores Under SDG 6.5.1 And The SDG 6.5.2 Scores. For Each Target Basin, The Assessment Shall Determine The Transboundary-related Score Based On The Four Transboundary Dimensions Of The SDG 6.5.1 Survey, Namely

Arrangements for transboundary cooperation,
Organisational framework,
Data and information sharing, and
Financing for transboundary cooperation.

In addition, the consultancy will assess the feasibility of achieving the programme's targeted 10% improvement in the impact indicator by analysing the performance of each scoring dimension, identifying key drivers, gaps, and constraints, and recommending strategic areas of focus to maximise programme impact and contribute to improved transboundary water management.

The baseline assessment will further validate existing programme data and evidence, generate robust quantitative and qualitative baseline information across the programme's intervention areas, and provide recommendations to strengthen the Results Framework, indicator measurement, data collection methodologies, and monitoring systems. The findings will serve as the reference point against which programme progress, performance, outcomes, and impact will be measured throughout the life of the CREATES Programme, while also informing evidence-based decision-making, adaptive management, continuous learning, and programme improvement.

Scope of the Assignment

The consultancy shall undertake a comprehensive baseline assessment and Results Framework validation for the CREATES Programme covering all programme outcomes, outputs, and indicators across the programme implementation areas in the Mara and Sio-Malaba-Malakisi (SMM) transboundary river basins. The assignment shall adopt a regional perspective and encompass relevant stakeholders at regional, national, basin, sub-national, and community levels, as appropriate.

The scope of the consultancy shall include the following activities, but not be limited to:

Review of Programme Documentation

Undertake a comprehensive review of all relevant programme documentation to develop a thorough understanding of the programme design, implementation approach, results framework, theory of change, monitoring framework, and existing evidence.

Baseline Assessment

The consultancy shall establish baseline values for all indicators contained in the CREATES Results Framework using robust qualitative and quantitative methods. The assessment shall generate reliable baseline information against which programme progress and results will be measured throughout the implementation period. Where baseline information already exists, the consultant shall validate its quality, relevance, completeness, and applicability before recommending its adoption or proposing updated baseline values based on evidence generated during the assessment.

Results Framework and Indicator Validation

Informed by evidence from the data collected during baseline assessment, the consultancy in consultation with CREATES programme team and MEL team shall review and validate the programme Results Framework to ensure that indicators are clearly defined, measurable, practical, and aligned with the programme's intended results. This shall include verification of indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, means of verification, data sources, assumptions, disaggregation requirements, frequency of data collection, and calculation methods. The consultant shall also develop or refine Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) for all programme indicators to ensure standardised indicator definitions and measurement. Where necessary, the consultant shall recommend revisions to strengthen the Results Framework while maintaining alignment with the approved programme design.

SDG 6.5 Impact Indicator Assessment

The consultancy shall establish basin-level baseline values for the programme's impact indicator, Achievement of SDG Target 6.5 on Transboundary Water Management, using the programme-specific methodology derived from the SDG 6.5 monitoring framework. The assessment shall establish baseline scores for each target basin by analysing the transboundary-related dimensions of SDG Indicator 6.5.1 together with the SDG Indicator 6.5.2 scores to generate the overall programme impact baseline.

new_jobs.location: Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
new_jobs.description:
We are currently looking for a Structural Conservation Senior Specialist
to join the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi.

The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) drives the sustainable growth of Abu Dhabi’s culture and tourism sectors. Through its work in cultural heritage, museums, historic environments, creative industries, and destination development, DCT Abu Dhabi plays a central role in preserving the emirate’s cultural identity while positioning Abu Dhabi as a leading global destination for culture and tourism.

Role Purpose

Lead the independent technical review, validation, and governance of structural assessments, material investigations, analytical models, and intervention strategies for modern heritage buildings across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Monitor and supervise structural interventions as required.

Key Responsibilities

Operations

Lead the technical review, validation, and quality assurance of structural assessments, material testing programmes, analytical models, conservation studies, and intervention strategies for modern heritage buildings, sites, districts, and urban heritage landscapes.
Assess and interpret the structural behaviour of existing modern heritage buildings, considering material degradation, historical construction practices, incomplete documentation, condition assessments, building pathology investigations, and historic fabric analysis.
Review and challenge consultant methodologies, assumptions, site inspection findings, testing results, analytical outputs, and recommendations to ensure conclusions are reliable, proportionate, technically sound, and aligned with conservation principles.
Evaluate and validate repair, strengthening, retrofitting, restoration, rehabilitation, adaptive reuse, and other conservation intervention strategies, ensuring minimal intervention, compatibility with existing materials, long-term durability, and preservation of heritage value.
Promote evidence-based and performance-based assessment and design approaches, including ASCE 41 where appropriate, particularly where prescriptive code compliance may lead to unnecessary interventions.
Ensure proposed interventions balance structural safety requirements with the preservation of authenticity, integrity, architectural character, character-defining features, historic urban character, scale, streetscapes, cultural values, and original material fabric.
Review and provide formal technical recommendations on structural submissions, including technical reports, review notes, presentations, specifications, method statements, restoration drawings, intervention guidelines, material treatments, and repair approaches.
Support the management of a portfolio of modern heritage assets under assessment by identifying priorities, risks, inconsistencies, feasibility requirements, viability considerations, cost implications, procurement needs, and adaptation or intervention proposals.
Supervise and provide technical input on site works related to structural improvements and conservation interventions, including monitoring structural status, site activities, logistics, mobilisation, and compliance with approved methodologies and DCT requirements.
Plan, advise, direct, and implement preventive and curative conservation interventions on registered modern architectural heritage, in coordination with relevant DCT functions, external consultants, and contractors.

Monitoring, Maintenance and Risk Management

Plan, manage, implement, monitor, maintain, and report on modern heritage sites in accordance with approved cyclical maintenance plans.
Coordinate condition monitoring, compliance monitoring, risk identification, enforcement recommendations, emergency planning, and corrective actions for deteriorated, abandoned, or at-risk modern heritage assets.

Policies, Processes and Procedures

Lead and contribute to the development of technical review frameworks, guidelines, procedures, quality standards, templates, and documentation standards for structural assessment and conservation engineering of modern heritage assets.
Provide technical expertise in defining acceptable approaches to code application for existing and heritage structures, including performance-based alternatives aligned with DCT objectives and international best practice.
Ensure technical reviews, outputs, and activities comply with relevant DCT policies, HED processes and procedures, international standards, and regulatory requirements.
Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to strengthen internal processes, review mechanisms, and operational efficiency.

Collaboration and Day-to-Day Operations

Collaborate with internal teams, external consultants, contractors, municipalities, regulatory authorities, academic institutions, and external partners on technical matters related to structural assessments, conservation interventions, policy implementation, and urban heritage revitalisation.
Support technical discussions with stakeholders and provide clear, defensible engineering positions for decision-making and project delivery.
Coordinate logistical operations related to permissions and site access for planned studies with site owners and stakeholders.
Maintain structured records of technical reviews, decisions, and supporting documentation in line with DCT requirements.

Research, Awareness and Capacity Building

Lead or contribute to research, innovation, publications, training materials, educational programmes, awareness initiatives, and supporting collateral related to modern heritage conservation, modern building materials, technologies, and capacity building.
Build internal and external awareness of appropriate structural engineering and conservation approaches for modern heritage buildings.
Respond to ad hoc requests related to modern heritage, conservation advice, reporting, stakeholder support, cross-functional initiatives, and any other duties assigned by the direct manager.
Contribute to the dissemination of knowledge within DCT and with relevant external partners, including workshops, technical forums, professional conferences, and academic events, as directed.

EHS (Environment, Health and Safety)

Comply with all relevant EHS policies, procedures, guidelines, and controls; report incidents and hazards in a timely manner; support employee safety and legislative compliance; and reduce consumption of natural resources to protect the environment and ensure a healthy and safe work environment.

Shared Activity

Follow all relevant departmental policies, processes, standard operating procedures, and instructions.
Demonstrate compliance with organisational values, ethics, and EHS requirements.
Support a culture of change management through a hands-on and can-do approach to DCT’s business opportunities, initiatives, planned targets, and high-performance behaviours.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or Structural Engineering.
Master’s Degree in Structural Engineering.
Professional certifications or memberships, such as PE, are an advantage.
6-8 years of experience in concrete repair and durability engineering, including corrosion mitigation and cathodic protection systems.
Experience in structural condition assessment of existing and ageing structures, structural modelling, and advanced analysis.
Knowledge of applicable codes and standards, including ADIBC/UAE regulations, ACI 318, ACI 562, ASCE 7, IEBC, and ASCE 41.
Proficiency with the following: ETABS, SAFE, SAP2000, AutoCAD, Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, etc.
Language competency in English is required; Arabic proficiency is preferred.

Skills

Technical expertise in structural assessment, material testing, analytical modelling, concrete durability, and repair strategy review.
Ability to interpret testing results and correlate findings with structural performance.
Strong judgment in reviewing consultant submissions and producing clear, defensible technical recommendations.
Knowledge of conservation principles, minimal intervention, material compatibility, and long-term durability for modern heritage structures.
Proficiency in technical reporting, documentation, stakeholder coordination, and structured record management.
Strong communication, collaboration, analytical thinking, problem-solving, and project coordination skills.

Interested candidates are welcome to apply or share their CV for consideration.

new_jobs.description:
𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗨𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗕𝗜𝗢𝗠𝗔𝗦𝗦 𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗧 𝗦𝗔𝗟𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗥 – 𝗕𝟮𝗕
Company: Rohit Exergy India Private Limited
Location: Delhi NCR
Employment Type: Full-time
Industry: Biomass Energy | Renewable Energy | Industrial Fuel
Function: Sales & Business Development

𝗔𝗕𝗢𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗢𝗟𝗘
Rohit Exergy India Private Limited is looking for an experienced Industrial Biomass Pellet Sales Manager to take ownership of B2B sales and business development for our premium-quality wood pellets used in industrial heating applications.
This is a hands-on sales role for a professional who understands the industrial biomass pellet market, has existing customer relationships, and can independently generate, develop and close business.
𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧: Prior experience in selling wood pellets to industrial customers is mandatory.

𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗣𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗜𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗘𝗦
• Take complete ownership of industrial biomass pellet sales and business development.
• Generate new leads independently and develop recurring industrial customers.
• Utilize existing customer networks and relationships to generate business.
• Identify industries currently using coal, LPG, diesel, furnace oil, biomass or competing wood pellets.
• Identify and develop opportunities for premium-quality wood pellets.
• Conduct customer meetings, plant visits and fuel assessments.
• Coordinate pellet trials and support conversion from existing fuels or pellet suppliers.
• Present the technical and commercial benefits of premium-quality pellets.
• Prepare quotations, commercial proposals, techno-commercial offers and customer documentation.
• Negotiate pricing, commercial terms and close orders.
• Coordinate with internal teams regarding product specifications, pricing, delivery schedules and payment terms.
• Track orders, deliveries, collections and repeat business.
• Build long-term customer relationships and increase monthly sales tonnage.
• Identify opportunities for pellet burners and industrial heating solutions.

𝗪𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗘 𝗟𝗢𝗢𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗢𝗥
• Direct wood pellet sales experience — mandatory.
• Existing network of industrial customers purchasing biomass/wood pellets.
• Proven personal pellet sales performance in MT/month.
• Experience selling premium or consistent-quality pellets.
• Strong independent lead-generation capability.
• Strong negotiation, closing and relationship-management skills.
• Understanding of industrial fuel applications and customer economics.
• Understanding of GCV, moisture, ash, combustion performance, fuel consumption and thermal efficiency.
• Experience with boilers, dryers, furnaces, thermic fluid heaters, hot air generators or other industrial heating systems will be highly valuable.
• Willingness to travel for customer meetings, plant visits and trials.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧 𝗖𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗘
We are looking for someone who can build business, not just handle leads.
The ideal candidate should be commercially driven, technically comfortable discussing industrial fuel performance, capable of generating business independently and confident in negotiating and closing B2B industrial sales.

Candidates with only generic B2B sales, commodity trading without direct pellet sales, briquette-only sales or unrelated industrial sales experience will not be preferred.

𝗥𝗢𝗟𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗧𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦
Position: Industrial Biomass Pellet Sales Manager – B2B
Location: Delhi NCR
Experience: Relevant wood pellet sales experience mandatory
Employment Type: Full-time
Travel: Regular industrial customer visits required
𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗘𝗡𝗦𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
Competitive fixed salary + performance incentives.
